The denial letter cites Aetna Clinical Policy Bulletin (CPB) 0286, stating that coverage requires "documented failure of maximally tolerated medical therapy and recent stress imaging consistent with high-risk anatomy," and asserts that the "submitted records do not include stress imaging within prior 90 days."

Furthermore, Aetna CPB 0119 supports the avoidance of redundant non-invasive cardiac imaging when definitive diagnostic criteria have already been established. 

The submitted left heart catheterization report definitively documents high-risk anatomy, specifically severe three-vessel coronary artery disease (90% proximal LAD, 85% LCx, and 90% RCA stenosis) with a high SYNTAX score. The ACC/AHA 2021 Chronic Coronary Disease guidelines provide a Class 1 recommendation for CABG in patients with severe multivessel disease and unstable angina to improve survival. The submitted invasive angiogram fulfills the CPB 0286 requirement for demonstrating high-risk anatomy, rendering the requested stress test both clinically redundant and medically contraindicated.
